source.title: Standard Treatment Workflow (STW) for Urticaria and Angioedema
source.publisher: Department of Health Research, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India

condition_description.urticaria: Sudden appearance of raised, itchy welts (wheals) on the skin of variable size and shape, surrounded by redness. Individual welts usually resolve within 1 to 24 hours but new ones may keep appearing. Chronic urticaria means it has lasted more than 6 weeks.
condition_description.angioedema: Sudden, deep swelling of the skin, often affecting the face, lips, tongue, throat, or genitals. It can take up to 72 hours to resolve. When it affects the throat or airway, it is a medical emergency.

sections.label: Emergency Signs: Call 112 or Go to Hospital Immediately
items: Swelling of the lips, tongue, or throat
Difficulty breathing, choking, or shortness of breath
Hoarse voice or difficulty speaking after swelling
Swelling of the airway (laryngeal angioedema), this is a life-threatening emergency
Respiratory distress combined with hives, this may indicate anaphylaxis
Shock: dizziness, loss of consciousness, very low blood pressure after exposure to an allergen

sections.label: Self-Care at Home for Mild Urticaria
items: Mild hives that are itchy but not affecting breathing can often be managed with an antihistamine prescribed by a doctor
Identify and avoid triggers: common triggers include certain foods, medicines (especially pain relievers like NSAIDs), insect stings, latex, and stress
Avoid common drug triggers if you have a history of urticaria: pain relievers such as ibuprofen or aspirin can trigger or worsen hives in some people, always inform your doctor of your history
Apply a cool compress to itchy areas for temporary relief
Wear loose, cool clothing to reduce skin irritation
Avoid vigorous exercise if exercise is a known trigger for your urticaria
Urticaria that resolves within 24 hours and does not recur may not need further treatment, reassurance is appropriate
About half of chronic urticaria cases resolve on their own within 12 to 24 months
Do not stop antihistamines abruptly if a doctor has prescribed a prolonged course

sections.label: See a Doctor
items: Hives that appear repeatedly over several days or are not going away
Any swelling of the face, lips, or eyes even without breathing difficulty
Urticaria lasting more than 6 weeks, this is chronic urticaria and needs evaluation
Hives that last longer than 24 to 48 hours in one spot, are painful, and leave bruising, this may be urticarial vasculitis, which is different from ordinary hives
Hives that seem related to a specific food, drug, or situation, allergy testing may be needed
Urticaria that is not improving with antihistamines
Urticaria associated with joint pain, fever, or feeling generally unwell

sections.label: Refer to Higher Centre
items: Any breathing difficulty, throat swelling, or signs of anaphylaxis, refer after emergency stabilisation
Angioedema affecting the throat or airway
Urticaria not controlled by standard antihistamines even at higher doses
Unusual urticaria: welts lasting more than 24 to 48 hours with bruising
Angioedema without urticaria, this may indicate a rare hereditary condition (C1 inhibitor deficiency) that requires specialist investigation
Urticaria with associated systemic symptoms (fever, joint pain, weight loss)

review.notes: All antihistamine names, dosing, injectable adrenaline protocols, and immunosuppressant regimens excluded. Emergency signs retained in full as they are triage-critical. The angioedema throat-swelling sign maps directly to the emergency banner rule.
